title: Family Assistance Legislation Amendment (Jobs for Families Child Care Package) Bill 2015
short_title: Family Assistance Legislation Amendment (Jobs for Families Child Care Package) Bill 2015

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would replace Child Care Benefit and Child Care Rebate with a new Child Care Subsidy, alongside additional assistance for vulnerable and disadvantaged families.
The main subsidy would depend on income and activity tests, with separate additional subsidies for circumstances including children at risk, temporary hardship and grandparent care.
It would also change provider approval and compliance arrangements and provide transitional rules for families and services moving from the existing child care payments.
changes: The applicable subsidy percentage would taper from 85 per cent to 20 per cent as combined adjusted taxable income rises across the income thresholds.
The Secretary could reassess service approvals from 1 July 2016.
Enrolment advances would close, with provisions allowing outstanding advances to be recovered.
summary.affected: Families using approved child care, children requiring additional support and approved child care providers would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Luke Hartsuyker
speeches.brief: The Family Assistance Legislation Amendment (Jobs for Families Child Care Package) Bill 2015 was introduced to create a simpler, means-tested child care subsidy replacing the current child care benefit and rebate, with subsidy rates ranging from 85% for families earning $65,710 or less down to 20% for incomes above $340,000. The package also includes an additional child care subsidy for vulnerable families, a nanny pilot program, strengthened compliance measures, and over $3 billion in extra funding, aiming to support more than 1.2 million families and prioritise low- and middle-income earners.
